why:
The divergence survives the challenge, but two of its evidence claims are wrong and must be corrected before it is used.

LEG 1 — QUOTE: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` -> line 507 contains the claimed text as an exact substring (Python `in` test = True). The claim truncates before the line's trailing `See [`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`](/docs/en/settings#strictpluginonlycustomization)`, which is a truncation, not a paraphrase. Not a refutation.

LEG 2 — CITED FILE:LINE: ONE OF THREE IS WRONG. In `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts`, `:177` really is `allowManagedHooksOnly` and `:203` really is `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, but `:129` is `readonly allowedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]` — an MCP allowlist, not a managed-only lock. And the OUR STATE sentence "We implement the per-surface locks allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly" is false for the middle one: `grep -ran allowManagedMcpServersOnly --include=*.ts` returns 6 hits, ALL of them prose inside comments (`sandbox-settings.ts:357,459`, `permissions-config.ts:1007`, `managed-only-locks.test.ts:236`, `managed-policy.ts:737,1321`) — it is not a field of `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and not in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`. Its absence is a recorded decision with a reason: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93` files it under "What we do not implement" with category `inapplicable — one tier carries these keys` — "Nessy has no user, project or local settings surface that carries allowedMcpServers or deniedMcpServers at all... Adding the key would declare a lock that enforces nothing."

LEG 3 — GREP -> 0 IS FALSE, BUT THE CONSEQUENCE SURVIVES. `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns 5 hits, not 0: `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:333323` and the four copies at `apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`. All are gitignored build output (`git check-ignore` confirms `.gitignore:7:dist`) carrying a vendored zod schema: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: preprocess(t => Array.isArray(t) ? t.filter(r => hU.includes(r)) : t, union([boolean, array(enum(hU))])).optional().catch(undefined)` with `hU = ["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]`. The string occurs EXACTLY ONCE per bundle, so the parsed field is never read by name — declared, not enforced. No first-party `.ts`/`.tsx` file references it (only docs do). So the identifier claim is sloppy but the behavioural claim stands.

LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — NO UPSTREAM HANDLER, NO SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CONFUSION. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (managed-policy.ts:501-534) is 34 keys and none of them locks skill or agent ORIGIN; `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727-733) drops any unknown key with disposition `stripped`, so an admin document carrying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is silently degraded rather than honoured. There is no second settings surface that could absorb it: the only `managed-settings.json` references are `managed-env.ts:27` (a comment), `self-config-deny.ts:74-87` (deny-path computation) and `managed-policy-loader.ts:57` (our `managed-policy.json` sits in the same directory). The surfaces the doc names really do load from user/project scope here: project skills at `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:485-486,523-524` (`PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`) and project subagents at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215` (`.claude/agents`) — gated only by the per-user trust/consent flow, which is a user decision, not an admin lock. Plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins`) narrow plugins, never user or project skills/agents.

OWNER-DECISION CHECK — NOT ONE OF THE NINE. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 lists SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not among them.

PRODUCT-DIFFERENCE CHECK — DOES NOT APPLY. This is not a dropped subscription flow, a gateway retarget or a rename. The fork invests heavily in exactly this surface (a 34-key managed Pi policy with `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `disableAllHooks`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`), so a missing admin lock is a gap in a surface we are deliberately building, not a scoped-out one.

PRIOR-REGISTRATION — PARTIAL, AND WORTH KNOWING. The gap is already noted in three places but never as a closed decision: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95` records only the `mcp` surface as `documented, not implemented — a settings key we do not carry`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46` lists it among admin locks and `:559` (R30) among skill/agent visibility controls; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-rules-tier.md:34` notes it has no `rules` surface. It appears in neither `2026-07-29-deviation-register.md` nor `2026-07-30-parity-report.md`, so the skills/agents half has no owner ruling.
correctedState:
`strictPluginOnlyCustomization` has no reader in first-party source: it is absent from `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and from `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534), so `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727-733) strips it from an admin document with disposition `stripped` (surfaced by `nessy-general-agent doctor`). NOTE: `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns 5 hits, not 0 — all in gitignored build output (`packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:333323`; `apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`), each a single occurrence inside a vendored zod schema (`union([boolean, array(enum(["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]))])`), declared and never read, so nothing enforces it there either.

The managed-only locks we ACTUALLY implement are `allowManagedHooksOnly` (managed-policy.ts:177), `disableAllHooks` (:191), `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (:203), plus `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly` and `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts). `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` is NOT implemented — it appears only in six comments, and its omission is a recorded decision: docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 files it as `inapplicable — one tier carries these keys` because no user/project/local settings surface here carries `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers`, so the lock's `true` state is already our permanent state. The `mcp` surface of `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is likewise already registered as `documented, not implemented — a settings key we do not carry` (managed-mcp-access.md:95).

What remains genuinely open is the SKILLS and AGENTS half: project skills load from `.nessy-agent/skills` (packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:485-486, 523-524) and project subagents from `.claude/agents` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215), gated only by the per-user project-trust/consent flow. No managed key forces either surface to plugin-or-managed origin, and the plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`, `deniedPluginKeys`, `enabledPlugins`) narrow plugins only. Listed as unimplemented in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46 and :559 (R30); not in the deviation register, not in the parity report, and not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3.
